models_evaluated: medical image classifiers (histopathology, chest X-ray, dermatology)

links.outcome: Subgroup diagnostic accuracy and robustness with vs without synthetic augmentation, in and out of distribution
links.effect: Adding diffusion-generated synthetic samples improved robustness in all three tasks and improved accuracy within underrepresented groups, especially out of distribution. Numbers not given in the text.
links.quote: Complementing real samples with synthetic ones improved the robustness of models in all three medical tasks and increased fairness by improving the accuracy of clinical diagnosis within underrepresented groups, especially out of distribution.

unlisted_practices: Using diffusion-model synthetic data augmentation to improve robustness and fairness of medical imaging classifiers for underrepresented conditions or subgroups

screen.reason: Evaluates generative synthetic data augmentation as a mitigation strategy/safeguard to address algorithmic bias and distribution shifts across demographic subgroups in medical imaging classifiers.
